final_claim: For the classical positive-parameter Lorenz–Stenflo system, if \(0<s\le \sigma^2/3\), the origin is globally asymptotically stable exactly for \(\rho\le 1+s/\sigma^2\), including the nonhyperbolic equality case.

correctness.rationale: The positive-definite storage matrix is verified on the entire weak-rotation range, and direct symbolic expansion gives an exact nonnegative-square factorization. Combining it with the exact (y,z)-energy identity yields a radially unbounded Lyapunov function. At the nonhyperbolic equality case, the largest complete bounded invariant subset of the zero-dissipation set is only the origin, so LaSalle closes the boundary. Above the threshold the linear characteristic polynomial has a positive real root.

originality.rationale: The local pitchfork boundary is established prior work and is not claimed as new. Inspected classical-system literature covers local bifurcations, boundedness and globally attractive sets, numerical dynamics, and controlled passivity, but no inspected source states the weak-rotation global if-and-only-if threshold, the explicit storage identity, or global attraction at the pitchfork equality. Two closely related later sources were available only through abstracts, so originality remains qualified to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The theorem upgrades a known local pitchfork boundary to an exact nonlinear global stability boundary on a nontrivial parameter regime and resolves the nonhyperbolic equality case. The transfer-function calculation also explains the weak-rotation cutoff as the point where the dominant passive gain leaves zero frequency, giving a structural guide for extensions.
